[{"id":5394792252,"body":"L1 attempted and **blocked before the lever could run** — not by anything in the extraction, and not by a state I can clear.

**What I did.** Dispatched Shepherd's scheduler with `wake: claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-baseline`. That worked: the run executed real jobs and reported

```
- woke #239 claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-baseline
- 2 item(s) pickable — the drain job dispatches an executor
```

missingbulb/Shepherd#239 is now `task:ready` and open, waiting for an executor.

**Where it stops.** Every `claudinite-executor.yml` run in Shepherd since ~11:48 concludes `action_required` with **zero jobs created**, about a second in — the drain's own dispatch (`github-actions[bot]`) and a dispatch I made directly as the owner alike. Nothing starts, so the item is never picked up.

**What I ruled out, by reading rather than guessing:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Account-wide Actions gate | No — a Claudinite workflow dispatched in the same minute ran its jobs normally |
| Shepherd Actions unavailable | No — Shepherd's *scheduler* workflow ran jobs at 11:48:26 and did real work |
| Private-repo minutes exhausted | No — Shepherd is public, same as Claudinite |
| An `environment:` approval gate on the job | No — the executor job declares none |
| Caused by this change | No — Shepherd has not converged yet; its mount is untouched, and its executor runs succeeded at 11:24 and 11:27, before the merge reached anything of its |

So it is specific to **Shepherd's executor workflow**, and it began between 11:27 and 11:48. That is an Actions gate at the repository level, and the tools I have cannot read approval state or Actions settings — so I am naming the boundary rather than proposing a cause I cannot see.

**What I did not do.** `fleet-baseline`'s only side effect per member is one dispatched scheduler run, so I could have hand-fanned that across the 14 members and reached L1's exit condition without the lever. I did not: it routes around the mechanism the pack exists to be, it is per-repo manual work of exactly the kind that reliably does not get repeated, and it would have left the real blocker in place and invisible.

**L2 (#1331) has not started** — it is gated on this.

Once Shepherd's executor can start a job again, the lever is one dispatch away and #239 is already ready and waiting.

`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

* Republish the dashboard when the mount moves, not only on a human push

The published site is stuck on claudinite-dashboard v10 while main's mount
carries v12, so the fleet grid still shows the "mount has not converged in
N days" verdict v11 removed. Nothing is wrong with the page: the deploy
never fires. Claudinite's update PRs are auto-merged by github-actions[bot],
and a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow, so every converge
lands without a build.

The catch-up follows the vendored scheduler, which is this repo's one
permitted cron, and asks on each of its wake-ups whether the page's sources
have moved since the last successful deploy — so the hourly cadence costs a
cache lookup rather than an hourly republish of identical bytes.

costs a stale page.

{"total_count":23,"workflow_runs":[{"id":32728354242,"name":"Claudinite scheduler","display_title":"Claudinite scheduler","workflow_id":336228270,"run_number":153,"run_attempt":1,"event":"workflow_dispatch","status":"in_progress","head_branch":"main","head_sha":"05bc710a34cef772bf9b8d5053e76350fd50d87d","head_commit":{"message":"Repoint the queue workflows at the claudinite-tasks mount, and name the secrets again (#258)

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331, missingbulb/Claudinite#1336

* Republish the dashboard when the mount moves, not only on a human push

The published site is stuck on claudinite-dashboard v10 while main's mount
carries v12, so the fleet grid still shows the "mount has not converged in
N days" verdict v11 removed. Nothing is wrong with the page: the deploy
never fires. Claudinite's update PRs are auto-merged by github-actions[bot],
and a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow, so every converge
lands without a build.

The catch-up follows the vendored scheduler, which is this repo's one
permitted cron, and asks on each of its wake-ups whether the page's sources
have moved since the last successful deploy — so the hourly cadence costs a
cache lookup rather than an hourly republish of identical bytes.

* Hash every generated artifact, not the roster by name

The already-deployed gate hashed `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` because that
is what this deployment's roster happens to be called — but the roster's
file name is per-deployment config, and a member list that changed under a
different name would leave the site serving the old one. The glob is
over-inclusive by design: an extra rebuild costs one run, a missed one
costs a stale page.

Keeps this file identical to the pack's stub below its header.

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

{"total_count":151,"workflow_runs":[{"id":32728401283,"name":"Claudinite executor","display_title":"Claudinite executor","workflow_id":336228267,"run_number":151,"run_attempt":1,"event":"workflow_dispatch","status":"in_progress","head_branch":"main","head_sha":"05bc710a34cef772bf9b8d5053e76350fd50d87d","head_commit":{"message":"Repoint the queue workflows at the claudinite-tasks mount, and name the secrets again (#258)

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331, missingbulb/Claudinite#1336

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331, missingbulb/Claudinite#1336

-# Claudinite work-item queue — the generator's scheduler run and its drain (tasks-dispatch
-# DESIGN §5, §10). This is the repo's ONLY cron, and it replaces the slot
-# scheduler's content at the same path when `taskScheduler.dispatch` is `"queue"`
-# — same file, same hashed minute, different mechanism, so the one-cron rule and

-#
-# A thin shim: all logic lives in the vendored engine, so this file changes
-# rarely. The cron line below is a placeholder; bootstrap and the wiring converge
-# rewrite it to this repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50 and its own two
-# anchor hours, computed by
-# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`.
-#

comments are inert, so no member can be carried anywhere by one, and demanding an
artifact for them is the cried-wolf firing the rule was deliberately narrowed to
avoid. It now compares both sides with YAML comments stripped and stays silent
when only those moved; a `#` still opens a comment only at line start or after
whitespace, so a `#` inside a scalar remains a real character, and a stub whose
head or base cannot be read stays a contract surface.

input.title: Drop the executor stub's comment about what not to put in it
input.body:
The secrets block in `packs/claudinite-tasks/stubs/claudinite-executor.yml` carried a paragraph explaining why the workflow does *not* serialise the whole secrets context. That is a note about an edit — #1336's reversal — rather than about the file in front of the reader, and the workflow stubs are the one surface where a comment is pure freight: every member vendors them verbatim, forever, and nothing reads them. The reason belongs where the decision is implemented, and [`converge-workflows.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq/packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs) already carries it beside the code that stamps the list.

What stays is what the block is for: what the converge writes there, and that it writes directly beneath the marker — which is why the marker is the last line.

The canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` is edited in the same commit, and the two whole files still differ only in the sanctioned places (the hand-maintained note, the hand-maintained secret list, and the repo-root `run:` paths).

## The check that fired on it

`consumer-safe-change` blocked this diff, asking for a migration record or a rehearsal fixture — for a comment deletion. A stub's comments are inert: no member can be carried anywhere by one, so that is exactly the cried-wolf firing the rule's own header says it was narrowed to avoid. It now compares head and base with YAML comments stripped and stays silent when only those moved. A `#` opens a comment only at line start or after whitespace, so a `#` inside a scalar (`echo 'a # b'`) is still a real character, and a stub whose head or base cannot be read stays a contract surface — the fail-safe answer.

Seen to fail first: the comment-only case was red against the old rule, and the earlier `check_the_work` run reported `1 blocking` on this same diff.

## Folders touched

```
.claudinite/local/packs/  consumer-safe-change ignores a comment-only stub diff,
                          with a YAML-aware stripper and four new tests
.github/workflows/        the canon's own executor loses the same paragraph
packs/claudinite-tasks/   the executor stub loses it; version 60824.3 → 60824.4
```

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → exit 0, 2731 passing, 0 failures. `check_the_work` → 0 blocking. `check_the_world` → 0 blocking.

Refs #1331

input.title: Drop the executor's comment about what not to put in it
input.body:
Regenerated from the canon's stub after it lost the paragraph explaining why the workflow does *not* serialise the whole secrets context. That is a note about an edit rather than about the file in front of the reader, and it is pure freight here: this file is vendored verbatim and nothing reads its comments. The reason lives beside the code that stamps the secret list, in the pack's `converge-workflows.mjs`.

Six comment lines out; the `# claudinite:secrets` marker and both stamped secret names are untouched, as is everything else in the file.

Follows missingbulb/Shepherd#258, which is why this is a second PR rather than an edit to that one. Canon side: missingbulb/Claudinite#1338.

Removed, everywhere it exists.

**Canon — [#1338](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1338)** (CI green). The paragraph is gone from `packs/claudinite-tasks/stubs/claudinite-executor.yml` and from the canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`; the two whole files still differ only in the sanctioned places. What stays is what the block is for — what the converge writes there, and that it writes directly beneath the marker. The *reason* already lived beside the code that stamps the list, in [`converge-workflows.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq/packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs), so nothing was lost by deleting it from the wrapper.

I didn't write a new rule for this: basics' *Writing a comment* already says to describe the current state and never the edit that produced it, which is exactly what I'd broken. A second rule saying it again wouldn't earn its place.

**A check got in the way, and I narrowed it rather than waive it.** `consumer-safe-change` blocked the diff, demanding a migration record or a rehearsal fixture — for deleting a comment. A stub's comments are inert; no member can be carried anywhere by one, so that's the cried-wolf firing the rule's own header says it was narrowed to avoid. It now compares head and base with YAML comments stripped and stays silent when only those moved. A `#` opens a comment only at line start or after whitespace, so a `#` inside a scalar stays a real character, and a stub whose head or base can't be read stays a contract surface. Four tests, the comment-only one seen red first.

```
.claudinite/local/packs/  consumer-safe-change ignores a comment-only stub diff
.github/workflows/        the canon's own executor loses the paragraph
packs/claudinite-tasks/   the stub loses it; version 60824.3 → 60824.4
```

**All 8 member PRs updated**, each as a second commit rather than a force-push, so you don't lose your place: [ClaudiniteCanary#251](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/251) · [ClaudiniteWebsite#297](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/297) · [CrosswordChat#313](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/pull/313) · [EdFringeNow#494](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/494) · [GoogleCalendarEventCreator#1055](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/1055) · [hitbut#117](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/117) · [VascularColoring#265](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/pull/265) · [WIP#96](https://github.com/missingbulb/WIP/pull/96). Verified per repo that the comment is gone and the `# claudinite:secrets` marker survives. Shepherd's had already merged, so it gets its own: [Shepherd#261](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/261).

**L1 finished** while I was doing this: **8 of 13 members reached canon**, 5 did not — LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR, and Shepherd itself (Shepherd only because canon moved again under it when #1337 merged mid-run). Up from 5 of 13 before the revert. Re-dispatching now would be premature — #1338 moves canon again, so the next sweep belongs after it lands.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **[#1338](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1338)** — the comment removal + check narrowing, CI green, awaiting your LGTM.
> • **9 member PRs** (8 above + [Shepherd#261](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/261)) — awaiting your LGTM; L2's exit condition needs them merged.
> • **4 members** (LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR) still short of canon; their L2 PRs follow once they mount the pack. Worth another `fleet-baseline` sweep after #1338 lands.

> • **[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** (PR D, shim removal) — held until L4; needs a rebase onto `main`.
> • **[#1333](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1333)** — the fate of `claudinite-canary-repo`.
